question:
A 87-year-old woman with a history of hyperlipidemia presents with a 6-month history of
activity-induced right-arm pain and achiness accompanied by localized muscle fatigue, which has
progressively worsened. She also reports generalized fatigue for the past 4 months. The pain is
triggered by activity and resolves with rest. She denies any smoking history. Two weeks ago, she
experienced transient vision loss in her right eye and underwent an unremarkable MRI of the brain and
ophthalmologic evaluation. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 126/80 mm Hg in the right
arm and 132/86 mm Hg in the left arm. A diminished radial pulse is noted in the right arm. Laboratory
tests reveal a normal complete blood count and chemistry panel, but her erythrocyte sedimentation
rate is elevated at 64 mm/hour (reference range, 1–25). What is the most likely diagnosis in this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Buerger disease (B) Atherosclerotic peripheral artery disease (C)
Fibromuscular dysplasia (D) Polymyalgia rheumatica (E) Raynaud phenomenon (F) Subclavian steal
syndrome (G) Thoracic-outlet obstruction (H) Carotid artery stenosis (I) Giant-cell arteritis (J) Takayasu
arteritis
 A. Raynaud phenomenon
B. Giant-cell arteritis
C. Atherosclerotic peripheral artery disease
D. Buerger disease
E. Thoracic-outlet obstruction
F. Polymyalgia rheumatica
G. Takayasu arteritis
H. Carotid artery stenosis
I. Fibromuscular dysplasia
J. Subclavian steal syndrome
